title: Candidate model showdown — decision log and leaderboard (Nov 2024)
content:
Purpose:
This note summarizes the November 2024 candidate model evaluation we ran to decide which model family/version to onboard as the next default instruction-following variant for Hosted API and Dedicated tiers. It captures the leaderboard results, slice-level regressions, prompt-set performance, and the recommended rollout plan with monitoring/rollback thresholds.

Background and motivation:
We have three candidate variants proposed by model-onboarding: rwf-alpha-2.7b (FP16), redwood-1.3-13b (INT8), and llamax-13b-qe (experimental quant). Primary constraints: keep median latency <= 320 ms for 512-token completions under continuous batching, target p95 latency <= 650 ms for Hosted, and not regress on our core instruction-following testset quality (measured by composite QA-F1 + instruction-adherence score). Cost per 1k tokens should be materially better than current baseline (redwood-1.2-13b), or we need solid tradeoffs on latency/quality.

Evaluation setup (short):
- Testbed: Dedicated small cluster (4xA10-like), runtime flags consistent with production serving runtime v2.1.
- Workloads: 3 prompt families: customer-support (500 prompts), code-assist (300 prompts), and longform-summaries (200 prompts).
- Metrics collected: composite_quality (weighted: QA-F1 40%, instruction-adherence 30%, hallucination-rate inverse 30%), avg_latency_ms (median), p95_latency_ms, token_cost_per_1k_usd (inferred), win_loss_head2head, stability_score (variance of outputs across 5 seeds), prompt-sensitivity (drop in composite_quality when instruction phrasing changed).
- Acceptance criteria: composite_quality >= baseline - 1.5 points AND p95_latency <= 650 ms OR composite_quality >= baseline + 1.0 and cost improvement >= 20%.

Quick leaderboard (composite scoring normalized to baseline=100):
1) redwood-1.3-13b (INT8): composite_score 108, median_latency 290 ms, p95_latency 610 ms, token_cost_per_1k $3.8, win_loss vs baseline 342-158, stability 0.06
2) rwf-alpha-2.7b (FP16): composite_score 103, median_latency 210 ms, p95_latency 480 ms, token_cost_per_1k $2.7, win_loss vs baseline 301-199, stability 0.08
3) llamax-13b-qe (experimental quant): composite_score 95, median_latency 350 ms, p95_latency 720 ms, token_cost_per_1k $2.1, win_loss vs baseline 220-280, stability 0.15
Baseline (redwood-1.2-13b): composite_score 100, median_latency 330 ms, p95_latency 700 ms, token_cost_per_1k $5.0

Notes on ranking rationale:
- redwood-1.3-13b wins on raw quality and has a modest latency and cost improvement over baseline thanks to improved kernel selection + INT8 pathway. It is slightly slower than rwf-alpha for median latency but hits p95 target.
- rwf-alpha-2.7b is the fastest and cheapest per token, but quality improvements are milder; shines on short instruction prompts and code-assist (code F1 up +4 pts vs baseline) but drops on longform summarization.
- llamax-13b-qe shows promising cost but had several failure modes on hallucination tests and missed p95 SLO; we consider it experimental.

Head-to-head win/loss summary (aggregated across prompt families):
- redwood-1.3-13b vs rwf-alpha-2.7b: 201-179 (redwood wins by narrow margin on longform and instruction-adherence slices)
- redwood-1.3-13b vs llamax-13b-qe: 275-105
- rwf-alpha-2.7b vs llamax-13b-qe: 230-140

Slice-level regressions and concerns:
- Longform-summaries (200 prompts): llamax-13b-qe median composite down by 8.2 points vs baseline, hallucination-rate increased from 6% -> 14% (regression). rwf-alpha-2.7b down by 2.1 points. redwood-1.3-13b +3.0 points.
- Finance/legal micro-slice (40 prompts): rwf-alpha-2.7b shows small hallucination spikes on table extraction prompts; redwood-1.3-13b stable.
- Code-assist slice: rwf-alpha-2.7b outperforms on unit-test generation but shows higher syntax churn (more edits per sample) — means more correct but less concise.
- Prompt-sensitivity: llamax-13b-qe highest sensitivity (avg drop 7.5 points when instruction phrasing varied), redwood-1.3-13b lowest (2.2 points).

Operational characteristics observed during runs:
- RW runtime kernels: rwf-alpha used continuous batching more efficiently (higher throughput), redwood-1.3 had better KV-cache reuse patterns for multi-turn sessions. llamax encountered occasional OOM under burst tests (tuned quant paths still brittle).

Decision recommendation:
Primary recommendation: onboard redwood-1.3-13b (INT8) as the new default instruction-following hosted candidate with staged rollout. Rationale: best composite quality, acceptable latency and p95 within SLO, measurable cost improvement vs baseline, and low prompt-sensitivity. It reduces customer-visible regressions risk while giving economics improvements.
Fallback recommendation: keep rwf-alpha-2.7b as the fast/low-cost tier available via model selector for customers that prefer lower latency/cost tradeoffs (exposed as model "rwf-2.7-fast" in the catalog). llamax-13b-qe should remain in internal experimental channel until hallucination and p95 issues are resolved.

Rollout plan (canary + monitoring):
- Stage 0 (internal): limited to infra tests, A/B harness — complete (this evaluation).
- Stage 1 (canary): 1% of Hosted production traffic for 48 hours; monitor composite_quality on live signals, customer support chatter, p95 latency, error rate, and hallucination alerts.
- Stage 2: 10% for 7 days if no alerts.
- Stage 3: 50% for 7 days, then 100% contingent on metrics.

Canary/rollback thresholds (automated):
- Immediate rollback if p95_latency increases > 15% vs baseline OR error_rate doubles OR hallucination-alerts > 2x baseline for more than 1 hour.
- Manual review required if composite_quality drops > 1.5 points on aggregated live evals or any severity-2 customer complaints referencing quality.

Monitoring hooks to add before canary:
- New perf dashboard tile: model_version, composite_quality (live eval stream), prompt-sensitivity heatmap per route, p95_latency by region, token_cost_by_route.
- Add lightweight on-host sampling: log 1 in 500 requests for post-hoc quality checks (redact PII by default).

Open action items:
- Engineering: stabilize INT8 kernels for full-serving runtime and run extended OOM stress tests (owner: Marco, ETA: 2024-11-20).
- Applied ML: expand longform prompt-set with additional 300 business-summary prompts to reduce sampling variance (owner: Tessa, ETA: 2024-11-18).
- Product/CS: prepare customer communication & opt-in flows for new model selector (owner: Riley, ETA: 2024-11-22).
- Observability: add composite_quality alert and hallucination-rate signal to Redwood Console for the canary channel (owner: Samir, ETA: 2024-11-16).

Appendix A — example prompts that flipped winners:
- Prompt A (longform): "Summarize the Q3 investor letter focusing on revenue drivers and risks; include expected runway implications."
- Prompt B (instruction): "Refactor the following function to be idempotent and add docstring + simple unit test."
- Prompt C (support): "Customer says their bill shows an extra $500 — ask clarifying questions and propose next steps."

Appendix B — raw leaderboard (per-slice highlights):
- customer-support: rwf-alpha-2.7b (comp 106) > redwood-1.3 (104) > llamax-13b-qe (89)
- code-assist: rwf-alpha-2.7b (comp 112) > redwood-1.3 (105) > llamax-13b-qe (90)
- longform-summaries: redwood-1.3 (comp 115) > rwf-alpha-2.7b (98) > llamax-13b-qe (82)

If there are objections to the recommendation, please flag on the Confluence page or escalate in #applied-ml within 48 hours. After sign-off, we'll schedule the canary per the timeline above.

Notes to reviewer (informal):
- We intentionally weighted instruction-adherence higher because we care about regressions that break integrations (tool-calling, structured output).
- For customers with strict cost constraints we should document recommended routes and a single-line note on caveats (e.g., rwf-alpha tends to be terse on long instructions).
- There are a few outlier prompts where rwf-alpha generates shorter but correct answers — may look like a regression in some tokenized metrics; keep human checks for those.

End of memo.
